chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi, from his father, from more than one person, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them both). He said:
Do not backbite, or you will be backbitten; and do not dig a pit for your brother, or you will fall into it yourself; for indeed, as you judge, so shall you be judged.

key_terms.تَغْتَبْ: Backbiting (ghiba) — speaking ill of a person in their absence; a major sin in Islamic ethics
key_terms.حُفْرَة: Pit/trap — metaphor for plotting harm against others
key_terms.كَمَا تَدِينُ تُدَانُ: As you judge, so shall you be judged — the law of reciprocity

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about backbiting and plotting against others?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delivers three interconnected ethical maxims warning against backbiting and scheming against others. The principle 'as you judge, so shall you be judged' (كما تدين تدان) is a well-known Arabic proverb expressing the law of reciprocity — what one does to others will return to oneself. This teaching was delivered in the context of the Imam's sessions (majalis) in Medina, where he instructed his followers on social ethics to cultivate a trustworthy and harmonious community.
word_analysis: may God have mercy on him
